package_info.package_manager: proprietary (commercial software, not public package manager)
package_info.package_versions: 2019.4 HF 5, 2020.2, 2020.2 HF 1 (and others released between March and June 2020)
package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion software was compromised during its build process, resulting in the injection of a sophisticated backdoor (SUNBURST) into distributed, digitally signed updates. This allowed attackers to covertly gain persistent, remote access to thousands of organizations worldwide, bypassing traditional security controls and code integrity checks by leveraging trusted software supply chain mechanisms.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (executed when the Orion BusinessLayerHost process starts)
execution_context.file_location: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (compiled binary, source code injected pre-compilation)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks if it is running in the Orion BusinessLayerHost process, then initiates a covert outbound connection to the hardcoded domain avsvmcloud.com, sending system and environment information, and if a command is received from the attacker, executes it on the host, enabling remote control and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code establishes unauthorized, covert network communication with an external, attacker-controlled domain, exfiltrates sensitive system and environment data, and enables remote command execution without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Orion DLLs should not contain logic that initiates outbound connections to undocumented, external domains or executes arbitrary remote commands. Such behavior is inconsistent with expected business logic and violates software integrity and security best practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate remote management or update tools may contact central servers for updates, but these actions are always documented, use trusted and verifiable domains, and are subject to audit and monitoring. They do not execute arbitrary remote commands received from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: Presence of hardcoded external C2 domain (avsvmcloud.com) in Orion DLL
Conditional execution based on process name (solarwinds.businesslayerhost)
Stealthy network beaconing that exfiltrates system and environment data
Capability to receive and execute attacker-supplied commands
No user interaction, notification, or logging of these actions

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains unauthorized access to SolarWinds build infrastructure, either via credential compromise or insider threat.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code injection during the software build process

attack_chain.action: Malicious code (SUNBURST backdoor) is injected into the Orion Core BusinessLayer DLL during the build phase, prior to compilation and signing.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is digitally signed and distributed as part of official SolarWinds software updates

attack_chain.action: Digitally signed, compromised Orion updates containing the backdoor are distributed to customers via normal update channels.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is installed and trusted in thousands of customer environments

attack_chain.action: Upon execution in customer environments, the backdoor code initiates covert beaconing to attacker-controlled domains, exfiltrates system and environment data, and awaits further instructions for remote command execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker achieves persistent, covert access and remote control over victim networks

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from the Orion BusinessLayerHost process to avsvmcloud.com or related attacker-controlled domains
Orion DLLs containing logic that checks the process name and conditionally initiates network beacons
Presence of remote command execution capabilities embedded within business logic DLLs
Stealthy exfiltration of system and environment data from Orion servers
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with unexpected code sections or non-standard hashes
Presence of digitally signed Orion DLLs matching known malicious SUNBURST hashes
DLLs containing hardcoded references to avsvmcloud.com or similar C2 domains
network_indicators: Outbound connections from Orion servers to avsvmcloud.com and related C2 infrastructure
Beaconing patterns from Orion BusinessLayerHost processes to external IPs/domains not associated with legitimate SolarWinds operations
DNS queries for avsvmcloud.com and other SUNBURST C2 domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected outbound connections from SolarWinds Orion BusinessLayerHost processes to known SUNBURST C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com). Perform file integrity and hash checks on Orion DLLs, comparing against known-good and known-malicious hashes. Analyze DLLs for suspicious logic, such as process name checks and network beaconing to external domains. Use EDR/XDR solutions to detect post-compromise activity, including remote command execution or lateral movement originating from Orion servers. Correlate network, file, and behavioral indicators to identify compromised systems.
